body:
Source: GitHub issue #599 (bug, P1-high, area:review). Re-verified on main @ 982adee7: packages/consensus-fix/lib/runner.mjs:71, `validateCandidate` returns `{valid: true, changes: parsed.changes}` unconditionally once the per-change loop passes — an empty `changes: []` array never enters that loop, so it is VALID by construction, and this is pinned by test/runner.test.mjs:120 `test('validateCandidate accepts empty changes array', ...)`. Consequence chain: an empty changeset applies as a true no-op (`applyChanges` iterates nothing), so a candidate's fate is decided purely by whether `--test-cmd`'s SECOND invocation (post-apply, on unmodified source) happens to exit 0 — which it will for any test that was red for an ENVIRONMENTAL reason on its first run (missing build artifact, cold cache, a fixture the first run itself creates). Every no-op candidate then survives and, because they all key to the identical (empty) changeset, they form the LARGEST agreement group with `changedLines: 0`, which also wins the smallest-diff tiebreak in `selectWinner` — beating even a real, correct 3-line fix if fewer candidates proposed it. `isAllDivergent` returns false (multi-member group exists) so the escalation-to-human path never fires. Reproduced end-to-end against the real runConsensusFix per the issue: 3 no-op candidates, a test command red-then-green, produces `Survivors: 3 | winner changedLines: 0 | winner changes: []`, renders "Winning fix has been applied" under --apply, gate exits 0 — nothing was fixed.

CONTEXT FOR THE BUILDER. Package `packages/consensus-fix`: bin/consensus-fix.mjs is the CLI entry. lib/runner.mjs holds validateCandidate (the function you edit) and runConsensusFix (the orchestration — step 6 builds `survivors` and calls `selectWinner`; read it to confirm where survivors are filtered, do not restructure it beyond what's needed). lib/agreement.mjs holds selectWinner/grouping/isAllDivergent — unrelated to this fix (the empty-changeset candidate must never reach this stage as a survivor, so agreement.mjs's own grouping/tiebreak logic does not need to change). lib/hunks.mjs, lib/region.mjs, lib/snapshot.mjs, lib/prompt.mjs, lib/format.mjs are hunk-application/prompting/output machinery, unrelated. Tests: `npm test -w packages/consensus-fix` from the worktree root. No cross-package consumer imports `validateCandidate` from this package (verified: packages/gate-fuzzing/lib/candidate.mjs defines its OWN unrelated same-named function; packages/cli, packages/core, packages/gate-manifest only mention the STRING "consensus-fix" in comments/registry/spend-category metadata, not a code import) — this fix is self-contained to packages/consensus-fix.

NORMATIVE BEHAVIOUR.
1. In `validateCandidate` (runner.mjs:49-71), when `parsed.changes.length === 0` return `{valid: false, reason: 'candidate proposes no changes'}` — BEFORE the per-change validation loop, as an explicit early check, not folded into an existing condition. Every other existing validation branch (non-object, missing/non-array changes, file not in allowedPaths, missing/empty hunks, malformed hunk fields) is unchanged.
2. The rejection reason string is exactly `'candidate proposes no changes'` (used verbatim in the new pinned test and in any --json / report output that surfaces `reason`).
3. Regression guard: a candidate with a NON-empty `changes` array where every change's `hunks` array is itself non-empty continues to validate exactly as today (no new restriction on valid candidates).
4. Rewrite the now-pinned-wrong test at test/runner.test.mjs:120 (`'validateCandidate accepts empty changes array'`) to assert rejection instead of acceptance, and rename it to describe the corrected behaviour — do not leave the old name on the new assertion.
5. Documentation: update `packages/consensus-fix/README.md` and hand-edit the same statement into `docs/tools/consensus-fix.md` and `apps/docs/content/docs/toolkit/consensus-fix.mdx` (mirrors — never regenerate) noting that a candidate proposing no file changes is discarded, not treated as a no-op winner.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA.
- AC1 `validateCandidate({changes: []}, ['a.mjs'])` returns `{valid: false, reason: 'candidate proposes no changes'}`. verify: `node --test packages/consensus-fix/test/runner.test.mjs`
- AC2 `validateCandidate({changes: [{file: 'a.mjs', hunks: [{startLine: 1, endLine: 1, replacement: 'x'}]}]}, ['a.mjs'])` still returns `{valid: true, ...}` (non-empty valid candidates unaffected). verify: `node --test packages/consensus-fix/test/runner.test.mjs`
- AC3 End-to-end: reproduce the issue's scenario (test command red on first run for an environmental reason, green on the untouched second run, 3 candidates all proposing `changes: []`) through `runConsensusFix` and assert the run does NOT report those 3 as survivors and does NOT select an empty-changeset winner — either they are discarded before the survivors stage, or `isAllDivergent`/escalation fires because zero valid survivors remain. State in the PR body which of the two actually happens. verify: `node --test packages/consensus-fix/test/runner.test.mjs`
- AC4 A real non-empty-changeset candidate still wins consensus normally when it is the majority/agreement winner (unrelated to this bug, regression-only). verify: `node --test packages/consensus-fix/test/runner.test.mjs`
- AC5 Existing suite green, with test/runner.test.mjs:120 rewritten (not deleted) to assert the new rejection — say so in the PR body. verify: `npm test -w packages/consensus-fix`
- AC6 Docs updated in all three places. verify: `grep -c "no changes\|no-op" packages/consensus-fix/README.md docs/tools/consensus-fix.md apps/docs/content/docs/toolkit/consensus-fix.mdx` (each >= 1)
- AC7 Mutation gate green on the branch. verify: `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12` exits 0 (also run `--max 80` once locally before review)

OUT OF SCOPE: lib/agreement.mjs's grouping/tiebreak/isAllDivergent logic (the fix keeps empty-changeset candidates out of `survivors` entirely, so agreement.mjs needs no change — do not touch it unless AC3's investigation proves otherwise, and say so explicitly if it does); the alternative fix shape from the issue (filtering zero-changedLines candidates out of `survivors` in step 6 of runConsensusFix rather than rejecting at validateCandidate) — this ticket implements the validateCandidate-rejection option.
title: consensus-fix: reject empty-changes candidates instead of letting them win unanimous consensus
